guide.h: What a good body paragraph looks like

bullets: Topic sentence: the main idea of the paragraph, linked to the question.
Explanation: why or how this is true.
Example or evidence: a specific case, a realistic situation, a consequence.
Link back (optional): how this supports your position.

guide.p: Each body paragraph should contain one central idea. If you find yourself writing 'Another point is…' halfway through, you probably need a new paragraph.

Coherence is about logic: the ideas are in a sensible order and the reader always knows why a sentence is there. Cohesion is about the language that connects them: linking words, pronouns and synonyms. Examiners look at both.

bullets: Adding: moreover, furthermore, in addition, what is more, also
Contrasting: however, nevertheless, on the other hand, whereas, although, despite
Cause and result: because, since, as a result, therefore, consequently, this means that
Example: for example, for instance, such as, a case in point is
Sequencing: firstly, secondly, finally, to begin with, subsequently
Concluding: in conclusion, overall, to sum up
Reference: use this, these, such, it, they, the former / the latter to point back to earlier ideas. 'This problem…', 'Such schemes…'.
Substitution and synonyms: avoid repeating the same noun — 'cars' → 'private vehicles' → 'they'.
Lexical chains: keep vocabulary connected to the topic so ideas flow naturally.
Starting every sentence with a linking word. Band 8 writing uses them where they help, not everywhere.
Using the wrong linker: 'On the other hand' introduces a contrasting point, not just another point.
'Besides' and 'moreover' at the start of every paragraph — vary or remove them.
Unclear 'it' or 'this' when the reader cannot tell what it refers to.
One-sentence paragraphs or no paragraphs at all.

guide.tip: Read your topic sentences alone, one after another. If they make a logical mini-essay, your structure is coherent.

models.title: Annotated body paragraph
models.prompt: Body paragraph from an essay answering: 'Governments should spend more money on public parks than on new roads. To what extent do you agree?'
models.answer: One important reason to invest in parks is their effect on public health. In crowded cities, many residents have no garden and few safe places to exercise, so a well-maintained park may be the only space where children can play outdoors or adults can go for a run. This matters because regular physical activity reduces the risk of conditions such as heart disease, which place a heavy burden on health services. A city that creates green spaces is therefore not only improving the quality of life of its residents but also, in the long term, reducing the cost of their medical care.
notes: Sentence 1 is the topic sentence: it gives one clear idea (health) linked to the question (investing in parks).
Sentence 2 explains the situation and gives realistic examples (children playing, adults running).
'This matters because…' uses reference ('this') to connect the example to a wider consequence.
'therefore' introduces the conclusion of the paragraph and links back to the writer's position.
Only two linking words are used, yet the paragraph flows — cohesion also comes from reference and logical order.
